subject: Biology
title: Skeletal Muscle Microanatomy & Sarcomere Architecture
learningObjectives: Diagram the banding pattern of a sarcomere from Z-disc to Z-disc
Identify the subunit organization of thin filaments (F-Actin, Tropomyosin, Troponin)
Detail the structure of meromyosin (HMM head/cross-arm + LMM tail) and its catalytic sites
content:
### 3.1 Structural Bands of the Sarcomere

```
                        SARCOMERE ULTRASTRUCTURE (Z to Z)
                        
          I-BAND            A-BAND (Dark)            I-BAND
        (Light/Actin)     (Overlap + H-Zone)       (Light/Actin)
     ├─────────────┤┌─────────────────────────┐├─────────────┤
     │       :     ││     |      |      |     ││     :       │
     Z-DISC  :     ││     |   H-ZONE    |     ││     :     Z-DISC
     (Line)  :     ││     |  (Myosin)   |     ││     :     (Line)
             :     ││     |      |      |     ││     :     
             :     ││     |    M-LINE   |     ││     :     
                          └──────┼──────┘
                          
     * SARCOMERE = Functional unit of contraction between two adjacent Z-discs.
```

1. **I-Band (Isotropic / Light Band)**: Contains Thin Filaments (Actin) only. Bisected vertically by a dense proteinaceous line called the **Z-disc / Z-line (Krause’s membrane)**.
2. **A-Band (Anisotropic / Dark Band)**: Extends the full physical length of the Thick Filaments (Myosin), including the peripheral overlap zone with thin filaments.
3. **H-Zone (Hensen’s Zone)**: The central region of the A-band containing thick filaments ONLY (no overlapping thin filaments present during relaxation).
4. **M-Line**: A delicate fibrous membrane running vertically through the center of the H-zone linking adjacent thick filaments together.

### 3.2 Contractile & Regulatory Proteins

```
                           MYOFILAMENT PROTEINS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   THIN FILAMENT (Actin Complex)                           THICK FILAMENT (Myosin Complex)
   ├── F-Actin (Double-helical G-actin polymer)            ├── Meromyosin Polymers
   ├── Tropomyosin (Covers Myosin-binding sites)           ├── Heavy Meromyosin (HMM: Cross-arm + Head)
   └── Troponin Complex (TnT, TnI, TnC [binds Ca²⁺])       └── Light Meromyosin (LMM: Fibrous Tail)
```

- **Thin Filament (Actin Complex)**:
  - **F-Actin**: 2 helically wound polymers of globular **G-actin** monomers.
  - **Tropomyosin**: 2 filamentous strands wrapping along the grooves of F-actin to mask myosin-binding sites at rest.
  - **Troponin Heterotrimer**: Bound at regular intervals along tropomyosin:
    - **Troponin-T (TnT)**: Binds Tropomyosin.
    - **Troponin-I (TnI)**: Inhibits actin-myosin cross-bridge binding.
    - **Troponin-C (TnC)**: **Binds $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions** (contains $4\ \text{Ca}^{2+}$-binding sites).
- **Thick Filament (Myosin Complex)**: Polymer of $\approx 300$ **Meromyosin** subunits.
  - **Heavy Meromyosin (HMM)**: Globular Head + flexible Short Arm (Cross-arm). Projects outward at regular intervals.
  - **Light Meromyosin (LMM)**: Fibrous Tail forming the central filament backbone.
  - **Myosin Head Functional Sites**: (1) Actin-Binding Site, (2) ATP-Binding Site with intrinsic $\text{Mg}^{2+}$-dependent **Myosin ATPase** activity.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Titin (Connectin) & Nebulin
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Titin is the largest known human protein (~3.8 MDa), acting as a molecular spring anchoring thick myosin filaments to the Z-disc and preventing over-stretching of the sarcomere. Nebulin acts as a molecular ruler stabilizing thin actin filament length.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Troponin Subunit Stoichiometry
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Every 7 G-actin monomers along the thin filament are associated with 1 tropomyosin molecule and 1 heterotrimeric troponin complex (TnT-TnI-TnC).
